title: Transporting a quadratic decomposition
statement: Let $m,n,k$ be nonnegative integers with $m=n$. Suppose there are $b\in\mathbb{F}_2$, a vector $a\in\mathbb{F}_2^m$, and two families of linear functionals $L_1,\ldots,L_k$ and $R_1,\ldots,R_k$ on $\mathbb{F}_2^m$ such that the combined family is linearly independent and, for every $x\in\mathbb{F}_2^m$, the complete quadratic bit equals $b+a\cdot x+\sum_{j=1}^k L_j(x)R_j(x)$. Then there are such a scalar, vector, and two families of linear functionals on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, again with the combined family linearly independent, giving this identity for every $x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$.
hypotheses_covered: There exist two families of $k$ linear functionals on $\mathbb{F}_2^m$
The combined family of functionals is linearly independent
The stated decomposition holds for every $x\in\mathbb{F}_2^m$
